R5B-bear-drive-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2021 (5 years old), right here: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2023 (fire C50354), 480 m SE: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
Unnamed wetland 100 m S: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

R5B-camp-camp-0002.recDirections: From Anahim Lake, travel south on Kappan Mountain Road (the turnoff is just west of the Anahim Lake Airport). Travel 5 km to the intersection with the Beeftrail Main FSR. Continue straight onto the Kappan Mountain Road for another 8.3 km and turn right onto the access road. Travel 3.5 km to the recreation site; the last 1.5 km of this road is fairly rough and narrow, and the final approach to the rec site is quite steep, and therefore a 4-wheel drive vehicle is recommended.
